TYPE OF APPLICATION: Administrative – Subdivision Plat Approval

 SYNOPSIS:
 On July 29, 2025, Fred Cox submitted a
 Plat Application to plat three (3) parcels.
 The parcel numbers are 16-31-101-005-
 0000, 16-31-101-023-0000, and 16-31-
 101-006-0000. The current land use
 districts of the parcels are Commercial
 Corridor (CC) and Commercial General
 (CG). The address for the project is 3432
 S State St, currently there are two
 operating restaurants within the
 parcels. This plat application is to plat
 and combine the existing parcels, so the
 landowner can build a new commercial
 building on the parcel. Mainly,
 commercial uses surround the
 property. The subject parcel currently
 subject to right of way easements in favor of Utah Power and Light Company and Mountain States Telephone and
 Telegraph Company, Cross-Access Easement to Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT). The proposed
 consolidated lot will be approximately 1.38 acres, meeting the minimum one (1) acre lot size requirement in the
 Commercial Corridor (CC) Land Use District.

 The Planning Commission is the land use authority over all Plat Applications.

 STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
 Staff recommend approval for a preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat one parcel.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:

Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the relevant
code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to approve the preliminary
subdivision plat amendment to plat three (3) parcels into one lot located at 3432 S State St., based on the findings of
fact, conclusions of law and conditions of approval for the subdivision in the staff report.


Findings of Fact:

     1. On July 29, 2025, Fred Cox submitted a Plat Application to plat parcels 16-31-101-005-0000, 16-31-101-023-
        0000, and 16-31-101-006-0000.

     2. The purpose of the proposed subdivision plat amendment is to plat the parcel for a new commercial
        building.

     3. The subject location 3432 S State St is in the Commercial Corridor (CC) and Commercial General (CG) land use
        district.

     4. The total development area of the three (3) lots is 1.38 acres.

     5. The minimum acreage requirement in the CC land use district is 1 acre.

     6. Section 17.07.010 of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code states that new buildings are required to comply
        with all IBC, IFC, development, and design standards.

     7. No impact is expected as part of the business on environmentally sensitive lands. There is no environmentally
        sensitive land on site.

     8. No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

     9. Commercial uses such as “Office”, “Restaurant”, “Retail” land uses are permitted in the CC land use district.

     10. Staff have reviewed this subdivision application for compliance with South Salt Lake Municipal Code
         Sections 17.10.120, 17.10.130, 17.10.140, 17.10.150, 17.10.160, 17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190 and
         17.10.200, and found that this subdivision application is compliant with this section, as outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

     1.   The plat and proposed use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City
          General Plan.

     2.   The plat and proposed use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with
          allowed uses in the CC district.

     3.   The plat and proposed use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or
          welfare of: Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the


                                                          10
          vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the proposed
          use or development.

     4.   The plat and proposed use, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on
          the citizens of the city.

Conditions of Approval:

     1.   The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior to
          recording;

     2.   Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must provide
          city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to dedication; obtain
          signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

     3.   The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant and post
          required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure improvements including
          street lights;

     4.   The curb cuts along State Street shall be consolidated per the approved Site Plan;

     5.   The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements of the
          South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;

     6.   The applicant shall dedicate a 10’ foot public utility easement to the City of South Salt Lake for purposes of
          storm water management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such
          easement, in a form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

     7.   The proposed development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community Development
          Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and the South Salt Lake
          Engineering department;

     8.   The applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire Codes and
          must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit;

     9.   The applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office within 2 years of receiving
          final plat approval or the applicant elects to install Infrastructure Improvements prior to Plat recordation,
          the applicant shall have applied for the proper permits, deposited a 10% Warranty Assurance and be actively
          working on the issued permit;

     10. All utilities shall be undergrounded.

     11. All items of the staff report.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends the Planning Commission approve, with conditions, a preliminary Subdivision Plat for a
one-Lot subdivision located at 3711 S State Street based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and
Conditions of Approval outlined in this Staff Report.

SYNOPSIS: SSLC OPC Venture, LLC, represented by Matt Connolly, petitions the Planning Commission for
approval of a preliminary Subdivision Plat, creating one Lot, to construct a VA Outpatient Clinic. The site
contains seven parcels, two of which contain Lots 11-23 of the Longview Park Addition Subdivision. The
Planning Commission will review the proposal to consolidate the parcels into a single 8.144-acre Lot and to
vacate the Lots from the Longview Park Addition Subdivision. Additionally, this Subdivision Plat will ensure
that the 200 East Right-of-Way (ROW) is consistent with the existing ROW line.

The proposed outpatient clinic is a Permitted Use in the Commercial Corridor. The Subdivision Plat is the
only land-use application required for the developer to entitle the project. Once the Subdivision Plat is
approved and recorded, the developer will proceed to obtain the permits required to commence
construction of the clinic.

REASON FOR REVIEW: The Planning Commission is the Land Use Authority on all Subdivision Plat approvals,
vacations, and amendments.

                                                     1
BACKGROUND

The proposed Subdivision consists of
seven parcels located at approximately
3711 S State Street. Five of the parcels
originate from the Pioneer-era Big Field
Survey (highlighted in red in the image
to the right). The remaining two parcels
along Secord Street are made up of Lots
11-23 of the Longview Park Addition
(highlighted in blue in the image to the
right).

The Longview Park Addition Subdivision
was established in 1910, encompassing
the Lots between State Street and 300
East, 3700 South and 3900 South.

In 1998, South Salt Lake annexed this
area, integrating the established
commercial area into the city. The site
has continuously maintained auto-related
land uses since the 1970s. Historically,
the property housed at least two
new/used car dealerships (1977-2012)
and an RV dealership (2018-2024). Currently, a portion of the property to the north is occupied by a car
rental business.

The Applicant, SSLC OPC Venture, LLC, proposes to consolidate all seven parcels into a one-Lot
Subdivision. This consolidation is intended to facilitate the construction of a Veterans Affairs (VA)
Outpatient Clinic (image of the clinic shown below), an associated parking garage, a surface parking lot,
and various site and landscaping improvements.

report.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY

         § 17.11.030 Land use authority designations.

Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

         A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of:
            Subdivision and Subdivision Plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision
            Plat; Conditional Use Permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in
            this Title; design review for projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any
            residential district; and the issuance of a Building or demolition permit in a Historic and
            Landmark District.

GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS

         Land Use & Neighborhoods Goal 3.
                     Enhance urban and streetscape design in the city to support South Salt Lake’s
                     distinct image and enhance community pride.

         Analysis:     The proposed Development will improve the streetscape along State Street, 200
                       East, and Secord Street.
ANALYSIS

   (I)      The one-Lot Subdivision, as conditioned, complies with the Commercial Corridor Zoning
            District requirements outlined in § 17.03.050 of the Land Use and Development
            Ordinance.

An outpatient clinic (medical office) is a Permitted Use in the Commercial Corridor (CC) Zoning District. The
following table outlines the requirements of the CC District and the proposed Subdivision’s compliance
with these standards.

        ORDINANCE STANDARDS                                             FINDINGS
 The minimum area for a new non-                Complies. The new Subdivision will create one Lot
 residential Lot is one acre.                   containing 8.144 acres.

 The maximum Height for any Structure is        Complies. The proposed clinic is consistent with the Large
 dependent upon the Building Form found         Format Commercial Building Form and contains 112,595
 in Chapter 17.07.                              square feet. Per § 17.07.110, the minimum Height is 26 feet,
                                                and the maximum Height is 36 feet. The proposed height
                                                for the outpatient clinic is approximately 34 feet. The

   (II)    The proposal complies with the parking ratio requirements found in § 17.06.160.

Medical Offices require four off-street parking spaces for every 1,000 square feet of floor area. According
to the application, the proposed outpatient clinic will have 112,595 square feet of floor area, which
requires 451 off-street parking spaces. The Applicant proposes 600 off-street parking spaces across the
parking garage (362 spaces) and the surface parking lot (238 spaces). The proposed number of parking
spaces will accommodate the VA’s parking requirements, which are more restrictive than Title 17, and
include 350 patient/visitor spaces and 250 staff spaces.

Additionally, the Applicant proposes to provide 26 bicycle parking spaces. The code requires one bicycle
parking space for every 25 parking spaces. Therefore, the Applicant is providing two more bicycle parking
spaces than required by code.

   (III)   The proposed Subdivision Plat, as conditioned, complies with the requirements of Chapter
           17.10, Subdivision and Platting, of the Land Use and Development Ordinance.

Pursuant to the City’s Land Use and Development Code, the purpose of the Subdivision application and
review process is to ensure the efficient, orderly growth, and beneficial Development of the city while
protecting the public’s health, safety, and general welfare. This review process provides a standardized
procedure for Platting and consolidating land to ensure that the resulting Subdivision has proper legal
descriptions, adequate infrastructure and utility capacity, and aligns with the city’s General Plan.

Prior to the Planning Commission’s review of a Preliminary Subdivision Plat, Staff from the Engineering,
Fire, and Community Development departments, along with Salt Lake County, review the Subdivision Plat
for compliance with the Subdivision and Platting requirements found in Chapter 17.10. After an initial
round of internal review, the Applicant is provided an opportunity to respond to these comments and
make corrections.

The following list outlines each section of the code and any corrections needed to issue Final Plat. The
Applicant shall continue to make all technical corrections prior to issuance of Final Plat approval.

   1. § 17.10.120 – Requirements for Improvements & Design.
                                                       7
           •   The petition complies.

   2. § 17.10.140 – Subdivision Development Lot Standards.
         • The Applicant shall ensure that driveways are designed and arranged to avoid vehicles
             backing onto surrounding Streets. See Analysis Section IV for further information.

   3. § 17.10.160 – Drainage, Storm Sewers, and Stormwater Facilities.
         • Approval of the Subdivision is contingent upon Compliance with the City Engineer’s review
             for this standard.

   4. § 17.10.170 – Water Facilities
         • The final civil plans for the project shall show the location of all fire hydrants and all water
             and storage supply improvements.

   5. § 17.10.180 – Sewer Facilities
         • The Applicant shall install sanitary sewer facilities as required by Mt. Olympus Improvement
             District.
         • The Applicant shall ensure sanitary sewer facilities connect with the public sanitary sewer at
             sizes required by Mt. Olympus Improvement District.

   6. § 17.10.190 – Utilities
         • All utilities shall be located underground.

   7. § 17.10.200 – Sidewalks, Trails, and Bike Paths
         • The proposed Subdivision complies with the Standard Road Profiles for State Street, Helm
             Avenue, 200 East, and Secord Street. A discrepancy with the 200 East ROW and the Salt
             Lake County Assessor’s Map will be resolved when the Subdivision Plat is recorded. The
             Applicant has dedicated 4,535 square feet of 200 East to South Salt Lake.

   (IV)    Traffic and Circulation Impact Study

Due to the site's proximity to the Residential (R-1) District, Staff requested that the Applicant conduct a
Traffic Impact Study to mitigate the impacts of vehicles on the surrounding residential streets. The study
was prepared by Lokahi, LLC, and is attached as Exhibit D.

The analysis shows that after buildout in 2028, the outpatient clinic is projected to generate 2,415 daily
weekday trips. Based on the analysis of trips generated at the site today, this is an increase of 1,653 daily
trips.

To further mitigate traffic impacts on the surrounding neighborhood, the study recommends that the
Applicant configure the site access points to accommodate increased daily traffic. Staff supports these
recommendations and has included them as a Condition of Approval.

The recommendations include:
   1. Construct a right-in/right-out driveway along State Street, approximately 335 feet south of Helm
       Avenue (centerline to centerline). The outbound approach must include a standard stop sign layout
       to slow vehicles turning right (north) onto State Street.
                                                       8
   2. Construct a right-in/right-out driveway along Helm Avenue, approximately 335 feet east of State
      Street (centerline to centerline). The outbound approach must include a standard stop sign layout
      to slow vehicles turning right (east) onto Helm Avenue.
   3. Construct a full-access driveway along Secord Street, to the satisfaction of the Fire Marshal, and
      include a standard stop sign for outbound vehicles.
   4. Construct a full-access driveway along 200 East. The exit approach must include a standard stop
      sign.

Because State Street is a under the jurisdiction of the Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT), the final
design, encroachment, and access are subject to their review and approval. The Applicant is required to
coordinate directly with UDOT to secure the necessary approvals and permits. Staff has included this
requirement as a Condition of Approval to ensure compliance with UDOT standards before issuance of a
building permit.

    (V)     The proposal, as conditioned, complies with the landscape standards in § 17.06.300.
As part of the Subdivision application, the Applicant provided a landscape plan for Staff review. While the
final form of the landscape plan is approved through the building permit process, Planning staff has
worked with the Applicant to mitigate loss of significant vegetation. Specifically, the site contains groves of
trees and shrubs toward the north and south ends of the Development area, as well as trees along the
eastern property line, as shown in the image below. For a more detailed view, please see Exhibit E.




                                                       9
§ 17.06.300(D)(2)(b)(v) requires the following:

Existing trees that are non-invasive and not noxious and that are preserved and incorporated into the
Landscape Plan shall be credited toward the minimum number of trees required by this Chapter. Trees
must be in healthy condition and free of injury to receive this credit. Any credited tree that is not preserved
or is significantly damaged during construction shall be removed and replaced with four (4) trees, each
with a minimum caliper of four (4) inches. Tree replacement shall conform to the tree and shrub
requirements.

To evaluate the Development’s alignment with this preservation standard, a comprehensive assessment of
the on-site vegetation was conducted. Because the Development will impact the trees, the Applicant
provided an inventory of each tree on the property and found the following:
    • Total trees inventoried:      428
    • Invasive/Noxious trees:       401
    • Non-invasive trees:           27

The non-invasive trees include Box Elder, Honey Locust, Callery Pear, Crabapple, and Northern Catalpa.
The invasive species, as identified by the state, include Siberian Elm. The applicant proposes to replace
the 27 non-invasive species with 118 trees throughout the development, which includes Bigtooth Maple,
Common Hackberry, Shademaster Honey Locust, White Oak, Woodward Columnar Juniper, Colorado
Spruce, and Amur Maple.

While the proposed replacement of 118 trees meets the requirements for replacement of non-invasive
species, the final landscape plan shall meet all requirements of this section and all commercial buffering
requirements prior to issuance of a building permit.

   (VI)    There is good cause to vacate Lots 11-23 of the Longview Park Addition Subdivision.

Pursuant to Utah Code § 10-20-812, the land use authority may approve the vacation or amendment of a
plat . . . if the land use authority finds that:
               a. There is good cause for the vacation or amendment; and
               b. No public street or municipal utility or easement has been vacated or amended.

Staff finds good cause to vacate Lots 11-23 of the Longview Park Addition Subdivision because doing so
will allow the Development of the site to support the health and well-being of a vulnerable population in
and around South Salt Lake. The proposed Subdivision aligns with the goals of the General Plan, utilizes
best planning practices, and protects the health, safety, and welfare of the community. Furthermore, the
vacation does not vacate or amend any public street, municipal utility, or easement.

PUBLIC NOTICE
Staff published notice on the City’s website and the Utah Public Notice website and posted notice to the
property on May 22, 2026. Staff mailed courtesy notices to property owners within 600 feet of the property
on May 22, 2026. Staff did not receive any public input at the time this report was published.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION

Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the
relevant code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to
approve with conditions, a preliminary Subdivision Plat for a one-Lot Subdivision located at 3711 S State
Street based on the Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Conditions of Approval outlined in this Staff
Report.

FINDINGS OF FACT:

   1. The property is located at 3711 South State Street in the Commercial Corridor District.

   2. The parcel numbers are: 16-31-152-003, 16-31-152-011, 16-31-152-012, 16-31-152-014, 16-31-152-
      015, 16-31-178-001, and 16-31-178-002.

   3. The parcels contain 8.144 acres.

   4. The property is currently vacant, with the exception of a parcel to the north, which is used for a car
      rental business.

   5. The purpose of the proposed Subdivision is to consolidate seven parcels into one Lot to construct a
      VA Outpatient Clinic, an associated parking garage, a surface parking lot, and various site and
      landscaping improvements.

   6. The proposal will also vacate Lots 11-23 of the Longview Park Addition Subdivision.

   7. The proposed VA Outpatient Clinic (medical office) is a Permitted Use in the Commercial Corridor.

   8. The proposed clinic is consistent with the Large Format Commercial Building Form and will contain
      112,595 square feet.

   9. Staff reviewed this Subdivision Application for compliance with the Commercial Corridor District
      requirements.

   10. The Applicant proposes providing 600 off-street parking spaces and 26 bicycle parking spaces for
       patients and employees of the outpatient clinic. South Salt Lake Municipal Code requires 451 off-
       street parking spaces and 24 bicycle parking spaces.

   11. The proposed development will remove 428 trees of which 401 are invasive or noxious species. The
       remaining 27 trees will be replaced with 118 trees, ten more than required by code.

   12. Staff reviewed this Subdivision Application for compliance with the requirements of Chapter 17.10,
       Subdivision and Platting, of the Land Use and Development Ordinance, and finds that the
       application is compliant, as conditioned below.

   13. The Subdivision will comply with all requirements of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code.


                                                     11
CONCLUSIONS OF LAW:

  1. The proposed Subdivision, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake
     General Plan.

  2. The proposed Subdivision, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in Use, scale, and
     design with the Commercial Corridor District.

  3. There is good cause for the Subdivision Plat, and no public street or easement is vacated.

  4. The proposal, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
     citizens of South Salt Lake.

  4. Approval of the Subdivision is contingent upon compliance with the City Engineer’s review of
     drainage, storm sewers, and stormwater facilities.

  5. The final civil plans for the project shall show the location of all fire hydrants and all water and
     storage supply improvements.

  6. The Applicant shall install sanitary sewer facilities as required by Mt. Olympus Improvement District.

  7. The Applicant shall ensure sanitary sewer facilities connect with the public sanitary sewer at sizes
     required by Mt. Olympus Improvement District.

  8. All utilities shall be underground.

  9. The Applicant shall design and develop each site access point and driveway to accommodate
     increased daily traffic as recommended by the Traffic Impact Study and as outlined in the Staff
     Report.

  10. Prior to issuance of a building permit or any work occurring within the State Street ROW, the
      Applicant shall submit to Community Development the necessary UDOT approvals for the
      improvements along State Street.

1. INTRODUCTION AND EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
1.1. PURPOSE OF REPORT AND STUDY OBJECTIVES
Lōkahi, LLC (Lōkahi) was retained by Molasky Development to complete a Traffic Impact Analysis
for the proposed VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic, located approximately 115 feet south of the
southeast corner of Helm Avenue and State Street in South Salt Lake City, Utah.

The objective of this Traffic Impact Study is to analyze the anticipated traffic related impacts of the
proposed development to the adjacent roadway network. See Figure 1 for the vicinity map.

1.2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The proposed VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic is located on the southeast corner of Helm Avenue
and State Street in South Salt Lake City, Utah. The development will consist of a Veterans Affairs
(VA) outpatient medical clinic with approximately 205 employees and is anticipated to open in 2028.

This Transportation Impact and Mitigation Analysis include:
    • Level of service analysis of existing conditions for the weekday AM and PM peak hours
    • Trip Generation for the existing development
    • Trip Generation for the proposed development
    • Trip Generation comparison
    • Level of service analysis for the opening year (2028) weekday AM and PM peak hours
           o 2028 No Build
           o 2028 Build
    • Queue analysis

The following are the intersections included in this study:
   • State Street and Helm Avenue/ Existing Driveway I (1)
   • State Street and 3750 S/ Existing Driveway II (2)
   • State Street and Rigdon Avenue (3)
   • State Street and 3900 S (4)
   • Secord Street and Rigdon Avenue/ Existing Driveway III (5)
   • 200 E and Helm Avenue (6)
   • 200 E and Rigdon Avenue (7)
   • 300 E and Helm Avenue (8)
   • 300 E and Rigdon Avenue (9)
   • State Street and Driveway A (10)
   • Helm Avenue and Driveway B (11)
   • Secord Street and Driveway C (12)



                                                                                                    1
                                                                                        Molasky Development
                                                                                  VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic


   •   200 E and Driveway D (13)

Existing Capacity Analysis
The AM and PM peak hour existing conditions capacity analyses were completed for the existing
study intersections.

The results of the capacity analysis reveal that all study intersections and movements operate at
LOS D or better, except the following:

       State Street and 3750 S/ Existing Driveway II (2)
          • Eastbound shared left-through-right operates at LOS E during the PM peak hour

       State Street and 3900 S (4)
          • Westbound shared through-right operates at LOS E during the AM and PM peak hour

Trip Generation
The trip generation was calculated based on collected traffic volumes at utilizing ITE Code 720 –
Medical-Dental Office (Stand-Alone). The proposed development is anticipated to generate 1,653
new weekday trips with 194 new AM peak hour trips and 87 new PM peak hour trips, compared to
the existing development.

Future Conditions - Year 2028
The proposed development is anticipated to open in the year 2028. An annual growth rate of 1.60%
was applied to the existing traffic volumes.

A capacity analysis was completed for both the AM and PM peak hours for the year 2028, without
the build out of the proposed development. The results of the capacity analysis reveal that all
intersection movements are expected to operate at a LOS D or better, with the exception of the
following:
       State Street and 3750 S/ Existing Driveway II (2)



                                                                                                                    2
                                                                       Molasky Development
                                                                   VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic


           •   Eastbound shared left-through-right operates at LOS F during the PM peak hour
           •   Northbound left operates at LOS E during the PM peak hour

The capacity and level of service for the study area intersections were evaluated for the 2028 build
traffic volumes. All intersection movements are projected to operate at a LOS D or better or will be
maintained at the 2028 no build level of service.

Recommendations

       •   State Street and Driveway A (10)
           o Construction of a RIRO driveway, located along State Street, approximately 335 feet
              south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

       •   Helm Avenue and Driveway B (11)
           o Construction of a RIRO driveway located along Helm Avenue, approximately 355 feet
              east of State Street (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the northbound approach

       •   Secord Street and Driveway C (12)
           o Construction of a full-access driveway, located along Secord Street, approximately
              460 feet north of Rigdon Avenue (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

       •   200 E and Driveway D (13)
           o Construction of a full-access driveway, located along 200 E, approximately 185 feet
              south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the eastbound approach

       • Monitor and Adjust Signal Timing
       It is the responsibility of the agency that owns and operates the traffic signals within the
       study area to monitor traffic conditions and make signal timing adjustments as necessary.

2. PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT
The proposed VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic development will consist of a Veterans Affairs
(VA) outpatient medical clinic with approximately 205 employees and is anticipated to open in
2028.

The existing RV dealership and rental car facility currently located on the site will be demolished
to accommodate the proposed development.

The development will be accessible via four (4) driveways:

State Street and Driveway A (10) is a proposed right-in/right-out (RIRO) driveway located along
State Street, approximately 335 feet south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline).

Helm Avenue and Driveway B (11) is a proposed RIRO driveway located along Helm Avenue,
approximately 355 feet east of State Street (centerline to centerline).

Secord Street and Driveway C (12) is a proposed full-access driveway located along Secord Street,
approximately 460 feet north of Rigdon Avenue (centerline to centerline).

200 E and Driveway D (13) is a proposed full-access driveway located along 200 E, approximately
185 feet south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline).

See Figure 2 and Appendix A for the proposed site plan.

3. AREA CONDITIONS
The study area is in South Salt Lake City, Utah. Sections 3.1 and 3.2 provide detailed descriptions of
the study roadway segments and intersections. See Figure 3 for study area.

3.1. STUDY ROADWAY SEGMENTS
Helm Avenue is an east-west roadway that provides one (1) lane in each direction of travel
with a raised median. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021),
Helm Avenue is classified as a local roadway. On Tuesday, April 14, 2026, a local traffic data
collection firm recorded 24-hour bi-directional traffic counts along Helm Avenue, east of
State Street. The recorded counts indicate an average daily traffic (ADT) volume of 869 vpd.
There is an unposted speed limit of 20 miles per hour (mph).

3750 S is an east-west undivided roadway that provides one (1) lane in each direction of
travel. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021), 3750 S is
classified as a local roadway. There is an unposted speed limit of 20 mph.

Rigdon Avenue is an east-west undivided roadway that provides one (1) lane in each
direction of travel. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021),
Rigdon Avenue is classified as a local roadway. There is an unposted speed limit of 20 mph.

3900 S is an east-west roadway that provides two (2) lanes in each direction of travel. East of
State Street, 3900 S features a center two-way left-turn lane. West of State Street, 3900 S is
divided by a raised concrete median. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update
(August 17, 2021), 3900 S is classified as a major arterial and is under the jurisdiction of the
Utah Department of Transportation (UDOT). The UDOT Traffic Statistics report that 3900 S
carried an annual average daily traffic (AADT) of 27,000 vehicles per day (vpd), between
State Street and 700 E in 2024. There is a posted speed limit of 40 mph.

State Street (US 89) is a north-south roadway that is part of U.S. Route 89 (US 89) and
provides three (3) lanes in each direction of travel separated by a raised concrete median.
According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021), State Street is
classified as a major arterial and is under the jurisdiction of UDOT. On Tuesday, April 14, 2026,
a local traffic data collection firm recorded 24-hour bi-directional traffic counts along State
Street, south of Helm Avenue. The recorded counts indicate an ADT volume of 29,843 vpd.
There is a posted speed limit of 35 mph.

Secord Street is a north-south undivided roadway that provides one (1) lane in each
direction of travel. Secord Street intersects Rigdon Avenue and extends approximately 540
feet north, terminating at a cul-de-sac. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update
(August 17, 2021), Secord Street is classified as a local roadway. On Tuesday, April 14, 2026, a



                                                                                                    8
                                                                        Molasky Development
                                                                    VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic


local traffic data collection firm recorded 24-hour bi-directional traffic counts along Secord
Street, north of Rigdon Avenue. The recorded counts indicate an ADT volume of 285 vpd.
There is an unposted speed limit of 20 mph.

200 E is a north-south undivided roadway that provides one (1) lane in each direction of
travel. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021), 200 E is
classified as a local roadway. On Tuesday, April 14, 2026, a local traffic data collection firm
recorded 24-hour bi-directional traffic counts along 200 E, south of Helm Avenue. The
recorded counts indicate an ADT volume of 438 vpd. There is an unposted speed limit of 20
mph.

300 E is a north-south undivided roadway that provides one (1) lane in each direction of
travel. According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021), 300 E is
classified as a major collector. The UDOT Traffic Statistics report that 300 E carried an AADT
of 6,800 vpd between 3300 S and 3900 S in 2024. There is a posted speed limit of 30 mph

3.2. STUDY INTERSECTIONS
At the direction of the UDOT and South Salt Lake City, the following intersections were analyzed:

State Street and Helm Avenue/ Existing Driveway I (1) operates as a stop-controlled T-intersection
with the stop control on the westbound approach. The northbound approach provides two (2)
through lanes and one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The southbound approach provides one
(1) dedicated left turn lane, two (2) through lanes and one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The
eastbound and westbound approaches each provides one (1) shared left-through-right turn lane.

State Street and 3750 S / Existing Driveway I (2) operates as a two-way stop-controlled intersection
with stop controls on the eastbound and westbound approaches. The northbound approach
provides one (1) dedicated left turn lane, two (2) through lanes, and one (1) shared through-right
turn lane. The southbound approach provides two (2) through lanes and one (1) shared through-
right turn lane. The eastbound and westbound approaches each provide one (1) shared left-
through-right turn lane.

State Street and Rigdon Avenue/ Existing Driveway II (3) operates as a stop-controlled T-
intersection with the stop control on the westbound approach. The northbound approach provides
two (2) through lanes and one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The southbound approach
provides three (3) through lanes. The westbound approach provides one (1) dedicated right turn
lane.

State Street and 3900 S (4) operates as a signalized intersection. The northbound and southbound
approaches each provide one (1) dedicated left turn lane, three (3) through lanes, and one (1)
dedicated right turn lane. The eastbound approach provides one (1) dedicated left turn lane, two (2)



                                                                                                  9
                                                                     Molasky Development
                                                                 VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic


through lanes, and one (1) dedicated right turn lane. The westbound approach provides one (1)
dedicated left turn lane, one (1) through lane, and one (1) shared through-right turn lane.

Secord Street and Rigdon Avenue (5) operates as a stop-controlled T-intersection with stop control
on the southbound approach. The southbound approach provides one (1) shared left-right turn
lane. The eastbound approach provides one (1) shared left-through turn lane. The westbound
approach provides one (1) shared through-right turn lane.

200 E and Helm Avenue (6) operates as a stop-controlled T-intersection with stop control on the
northbound approach. The northbound approach provides one (1) shared left-right turn lane. The
eastbound approach provides one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The westbound approach
provides one (1) shared left-through turn lane.

200 E and Rigdon Avenue (7) operates as a four-way stop controlled intersection. Each approach
provides one (1) shared left-through-right turn lane.

300 E and Helm Avenue (8) operates as a one-way stop-controlled T-intersection with stop control
on the eastbound approach. The northbound approach provides one (1) shared left-through turn
lane. The southbound approach provides one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The eastbound
approach provides one (1) shared left-right turn lane.

300 E and Rigdon Avenue (9) operates as a one-way stop-controlled T-intersection with stop
control on the eastbound approach. The northbound approach provides one (1) shared left-through
turn lane. The southbound approach provides one (1) shared through-right turn lane. The
eastbound approach provides one (1) shared left-right turn lane.

3.3. SURROUNDING AREA LAND USE
The proposed development is in South Salt Lake City, Utah. The proposed development is bordered
by single-family homes, a medical clinic, and Helm Avenue to the north; Rigdon Avenue, single-
family homes and commercial uses to the south; 200 E and single-family homes to the west; Secord
Street, State Street, and single-family homes to the east.

Surrounding land use generally consists of residential and commercial use.

3.4.SITE ACCESSIBILITY
Roadway System
US 89 (State Street) runs directly along to the site’s western frontage, providing regional
connectivity to the Salt Lake City metropolitan area and interstate access to Arizona and Montana.
Within the vicinity of the proposed site, there is a well-developed roadway network.

Pedestrian Facilities
Sidewalks are provided along all study roadway segments within the study area.

Marked crosswalks are provided across all legs of State Street and 3900 S (4) and the southern leg
of 300 E and Helm Avenue (8).

There are no other pedestrian facilities currently provided within the study area.

Bicycle Facilities
Bike lanes are not currently provided within the study area.

Transit Facilities
The Utah Transit Authority (UTA) provides public transportation within the study area and serves
the Salt Lake City metropolitan area.

UTA Route 39, which provides east-west service, and Route 200, which provides north-south
service, operate within the immediate study area and are both located within a 10-miute walking
distance of the proposed development.

4.3.EXISTING CAPACITY ANALYSIS
The existing conditions capacity analysis was completed for the existing study intersections using
the methodology presented in the 7th Edition of the Highway Capacity Manual (HCM). Traffic analysis
software, Synchro Version 12, was used to perform the analyses based on signal timing provided by
the Utah Department of Transportation. Existing peak hour factors (PHF) were used. U turn
movements were evaluated as left turns as Synchro does not explicitly analyze U turns. See
Appendix D for the existing signal timing.

Table 1 is from the 7th Edition of the Highway Capacity Manual Exhibit 19-8 and 20-2, which lists the
Level of Service (LOS) thresholds for signalized and stop-controlled intersections.

                                    Table 1 – Level of Service Criteria

                                                   Control Delay per Vehicle (s/veh)
                Level of Service (LOS)
                                         Signalized Intersection     Unsignalized Intersection
                          A                        ≤ 10                          0 - 10
                          B                      > 10-20                        > 10-15
                          C                      > 20-35                       > 15-25
                          D                      > 35-55                       > 25-35
                          E                      > 55-80                       > 35-50
                          F                       > 80                           > 50

The results of the capacity analysis reveal that all the study intersections and movements operate at
LOS D or better, except the following:

       State Street and 3750 S/ Existing Driveway II (2)
          • Eastbound shared left-through-right operates at LOS E during the PM peak hour

       State Street and 3900 S (4)
          • Westbound shared through-right operates at LOS E during the AM and PM peak hour

See Figure 5 for the existing AM and PM peak hour capacity analysis. The detailed capacity analysis
sheets can be found in Appendix E.

5. PROJECTED TRAFFIC
5.1. TRIP GENERATION
The trip generation for the proposed development was calculated utilizing the Institute of
Transportation Engineers (ITE) publication entitled Trip Generation Manual, 12th Edition. This
publication is the standard for the transportation engineering profession. Detailed trip generation
calculations are provided in Appendix F.

5.1.1. TRIP GENERATION - PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT
The trip generation of the proposed development was calculated utilizing ITE Code 720 – Medical-
Dental Office (Stand-Alone). The trip generation calculations of the proposed development are
shown in Table 1.

                             Table 2 – Trip Generation - Proposed Development

                                          ITE                        Weekday     AM Peak Hour    PM Peak Hour
                Land Use                         Qty       Unit
                                         Code                         Total    Total In    Out Total In    Out
      Medical-Dental Office Building
                                          720    205     Employees    2,415    254   178   76   193   87   106
              (Stand-Alone)

The proposed development is anticipated to generate a total of 2,415 new daily weekday trips with
254 trips during the AM peak hour and 193 trips during the PM peak hour.

6. FUTURE CONDITIONS (YEAR 2028)
The proposed development is scheduled for opening and completion in the year 2028. This section
analyzes the anticipated impacts of the proposed development on the surrounding roadway
network during the opening year 2028.

6.1. YEAR 2028 ROADWAY NETWORK
The roadway improvements described below are anticipated to be implemented in 2028 in
conjunction with the buildout of the proposed development. All improvements will be the
responsibility of the developer.

State Street and Driveway A (10)
   • Construction of a RIRO driveway, located along State Street, approximately 335 feet south
       of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
   • Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

Helm Avenue and Driveway B (11)
   • Construction of a RIRO driveway located along Helm Avenue, approximately 355 feet east of
      State Street (centerline to centerline)
   • Installation of a stop sign on the northbound approach

Secord Street and Driveway C (12)
   • Construction of a full-access driveway, located along Secord Street, approximately 460 feet
      north of Rigdon Avenue (centerline to centerline)
   • Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

200 E and Driveway D (13)
   • Construction of a full-access driveway, located along 200 E, approximately 185 feet south of
       Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
   • Installation of a stop sign on the eastbound approach

6.2.YEAR 2028 NO BUILD TRAFFIC VOLUMES
According to the South Salt Lake General Plan Update (August 17, 2021), South Salt Lake City had a
population of 26,794 in 2020. It is projected that the population will reach 36,638 in the year 2040.
This results in an average annual growth rate of 1.6%. Accordingly, an 1.6% annual growth rate will
be applied to existing traffic counts to project future traffic volumes.

See Figure 8 for the year 2028 no build traffic volumes.

6.3.YEAR 2028 BUILD TRAFFIC VOLUMES
When the site traffic volumes (Figure 7) are added to the 2028 no build traffic volumes (Figure 8),
the result is the 2028 build traffic volumes. The year 2028 build traffic volumes are shown in Figure
9.

6.4. YEAR 2028 NO BUILD CAPACITY ANALYSIS
The capacity and level of service for the study area intersections were evaluated for the 2028 no
build traffic volumes (Figure 8). The signal timing splits were adjusted for future traffic volumes,
and the PHFs for future conditions were assumed to be 0.92 as directed by South Salt Lake City
staff.

The results of the year 2028 no build capacity analysis are shown in Figure 10. The results of the
capacity analysis reveal that all movements are expected to operate at a LOS D or better, with the
exception of the following:

State Street and 3750 S/ Existing Driveway II (2)
           • Eastbound shared left-through-right operates at LOS F during the PM peak hour
           • Northbound left operates at LOS E during the PM peak hour

This condition is typical of unsignalized access points on high volume roadways, where heavily
opposing traffic limits acceptable gaps for left turns during peak periods. As a result, increased
delays are expected. Drivers may adjust by using alternative routes, reducing demand for these
constrained movements.

The detailed capacity analysis sheets can be found in Appendix G.

6.5.   YEAR 2028 BUILD CAPACITY ANALYSIS
The capacity and level of service for the study area intersections were evaluated for the year 2028
build traffic volumes (Figure 9). The signal timing splits were adjusted for future traffic volumes,
and the PHFs for future conditions were assumed to be 0.92 as directed by South Salt Lake City
staff.

The results of the year 2028 build capacity analysis are shown in Figure 11. All movements are
expected to operate at a LOS D or better or are maintained at the 2028 no build level of service.

The detailed capacity analysis sheets can be found in Appendix H.

8. RECOMMENDATIONS & CONCLUSIONS
The proposed VA Salt Lake City Outpatient Clinic development will consist of a Veterans Affairs (VA)
outpatient medical clinic with approximately 205 employees and is anticipated to open in 2028.

Operational analysis indicates that all existing access points are expected to operate at acceptable
levels of service under 2028 build year conditions. The existing turn lane storage lengths provide
sufficient storage to accommodate the projected site traffic volumes.

The proposed development is anticipated to generate 1,653 new weekday trips with 194 new AM
peak hour trips and 87 new PM peak hour trips, compared to the existing development.

The following is recommended:
       • State Street and Driveway A (10)
          o Construction of a RIRO driveway, located along State Street, approximately 335 feet
              south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
          o Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

       •   Helm Avenue and Driveway B (11)
           o Construction of a RIRO driveway located along Helm Avenue, approximately 355 feet
              east of State Street (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the northbound approach

       •   Secord Street and Driveway C (12)
           o Construction of a full-access driveway, located along Secord Street, approximately
              460 feet north of Rigdon Avenue (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the westbound approach

       •   200 E and Driveway D (13)
           o Construction of a full-access driveway, located along 200 E, approximately 185 feet
              south of Helm Avenue (centerline to centerline)
           o Installation of a stop sign on the eastbound approach

       • Monitor and Adjust Signal Timing
       It is the responsibility of the agency that operates the traffic signals in the study area to
       monitor traffic patterns and make any signal timing adjustments, as necessary.
